name: King of Pentacles
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: finished full-bleed portrait illustration for one card of the Earth Warden tarot deck. Style: luminous mythic fantasy painting, richly detailed and painterly, collectible quality. Ancient wild places lit from within: glowing moss and fungi, drifting fireflies and motes of light, shafts of light through old trees, soft aurora over stone. Palette: moss and fern green, deep loam brown, lichen grey, warm amber and antique gold, with pale luminous green-gold and moon-white accents; dark, rich and glowing overall. Every human figure is a woman: wardens of the land, of varied ages, builds and skin tones, dignified and capable, fully clothed in practical layered garments of wool, linen, leather and woven grasses with gold and stone ornaments. Faces are natural and expressive; hands are well formed with five fingers. Composition: one clear scene, the main figure or object large and central, readable at small size, the whole subject inside the frame with a little quiet space at every edge. When the scene gives an exact number of objects, show exactly that many, each one separate and easy to count. This is the complete artwork seen straight on, not a photograph of a card and not a mockup. No text, no letters, no numbers, no Roman numerals, no runes or writing of any kind, no labels, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame, no card outline. In this deck a pentacle is a round disc of gold and carved stone, about the size of a plate, bearing a five-petalled flower carved in its face.
Card: KING OF PENTACLES.
Scene: A sovereign woman in a robe embroidered with grapes and vines sits on a throne carved with bulls' heads, a sceptre in one hand and one round disc resting on her knee beneath the other hand. Castle walls and gardens behind her. Exactly one disc. Stewardship and material mastery.
